Brownsville is seeing major new investment in shipbuilding, energy, space, and advanced manufacturing.

Twenty-five years after the devastating September 11 terrorist attacks on our nation, we continue to confront an evolving terrorism landscape that demands an equally dynamic counterterrorism response. Since that day, we have worked to ensure that an attack like 9/11 never happens again. We must continue that work by strengthening partnerships with allies and partners overseas, disrupting terrorist networks and their proxies, and doing everything we can to keep Americans safe.

Terrorism can emerge from anywhere, and our counterterrorism efforts must reflect that reality. Our resources, strategies, and partnerships should not be narrowly focused on a handful of designated areas. Instead, we must cast a broad net to identify, disrupt, and counter terrorist threats wherever they emerge.

text: I strongly support the people of Ukraine. I have consistently spoken out against Russian aggression and have voted for funding to assist Ukraine in fighting the war. For many seniors and patients in South Texas, home health care means being able to get the care they need without leaving their home.

I sat down with representatives from the Texas Association for Home Care and Hospice to discuss the federal policies affecting home health providers and the patients they serve.

We talked about CMS’s proposed 2027 home health payment rule and concerns about how changes to Medicare payment policies could affect access to care across Texas. CMS is currently considering several payment and policy changes for home health agencies beginning next year.

Home health and hospice providers care for seniors, people with disabilities, and families during some of the most difficult times in their lives. I will continue working to protect access to care and make sure Medicare policies work for patients and the providers who serve them.

We discussed the key factors that keep trade moving, including commercial lane availability, CBP operations, inspection procedures, staffing, technology, and delays affecting trucks crossing the bridge.

Eagle Pass relies on efficient bridge operations to support local businesses, cross-border trade, and families traveling between the United States and Mexico.

Border security and trade must work together.

I will continue working with the City of Eagle Pass, Maverick County, CBP, and federal partners to help ensure the community has the staffing, technology, and resources needed to support secure and efficient bridge operations.

Community health workers help connect patients with the care and services they need, especially in rural and underserved communities.

I spoke with representatives from Methodist Healthcare Ministries of South Texas about their work to improve access to care across South Texas and the challenges facing the communities they serve.

We discussed expanding access to community health workers, changes in federal grant funding, and the importance of broadband and digital literacy. In rural communities, reliable internet can make a real difference in whether families can access telehealth, health information, and other important services.

I will continue working to strengthen access to health care, expand broadband access, and support the organizations serving families across South Texas.

Young people should know what to do when an emergency happens at school, at home, or in their community.

I spoke with Dustin and Michelle Titzman, co-founders of Warrior Kid Medic, about their work to teach students practical emergency response skills and prepare them to act when something goes wrong.

They are working to launch a youth preparedness pilot program in schools across South Texas. We discussed how the program could work with existing school safety and emergency preparedness efforts and how to measure its impact on students.

Giving students the skills to stay calm, make good decisions, and help others can make our schools and communities safer. I will continue working to support school safety and emergency preparedness efforts across South Texas.

I strongly support the use of targeted sanctions to cut off funding for Putin’s devastating attacks; however, I can’t vote for a bill that hands Donald Trump sweeping new tariff authority that he will undoubtedly abuse and hurt my constituents even more.

Ukrainians deserve a clean bill that supports their country’s defense and their fight for democracy abroad, not a bill that allows Trump to roll back sanctions and ratchet up his devastating trade war.

urls.description: Congress is poised to deliver President Donald Trump one final win ahead of the midterms — a major Russia sanctions bill that critics warn will empower him to impose sweeping new tariffs that could reverberate across the economy.
urls.title: Some Republicans privately fear Russia sanctions bill will give Trump too much power on tariffs | CNN Politics

text: Tonight, I voted for even harsher sanctions on Russia. Every bomb we can stop Putin from buying is an innocent Ukrainian life we can save. I stand firmly with the Ukrainian people in their fight to protect democracy and end Putin’s fascist aggression.

text:
I wholeheartedly support the Ukrainian people as they continue to stand against an illegal Russian invasion. Putin must immediately end his aggression, and the US must use our leverage to push for peace and security for the Ukrainian people.

Today, I voted NO on the Lindsay O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act as it grants President Trump incredibly broad authority to impose tariffs and does not include necessary safeguards to ensure Trump uses these new tariff authorities to end the war. Trump has repeatedly abused tariffs to exact revenge for petty grievances, devoid of any true strategy, and we have no reason to believe he will use this new tariff authority any differently.

After over four years of war, the Ukrainian people deserve peace. I will continue doing everything in my power to ensure peace and security for Ukraine.
